issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Meal class with a constructor Meal(String, String[]). However, the template repository contains an empty Meal.java and instead provides an Order class that has the expected constructor and API. This name/constructor discrepancy (Meal missing, Order present) will confuse students: they will be instructed to work with Meal but the template examples and provided starter code use Order. Students may implement Meal but still find template examples referencing Order, or they may be unsure which class to modify.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement by providing a Meal class with the constructor Meal(String, String[]) (matching the solution). Concretely either: (a) rename or duplicate the existing Order class to Meal (and remove or adapt Order), or (b) add a proper Meal.java implementation (copying the Order API) and update the template Main and any comments to reference Meal. Ensure the empty Meal.java in the template is replaced with the proper constructor and getters so students have the expected starting point.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the core domain entity as 'Meal' (class Meal with getName/getIngredients, methods in SealSaloon operate on Meal), but the template repository provides an 'Order' class with the same structure and semantics. This mismatch (Meal vs Order) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the exercise expect a Meal class to exist and to be used by SealSaloon, yet the starter code names that entity Order and the Meal.java file is empty. They may search for or attempt to modify Meal.java (as described in the task) and not find the expected implementation, causing unnecessary confusion and extra cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts: either rename the template's Order class to Meal (move/rename src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java -> src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) and populate Meal.java accordingly, and update any references (e.g., Main) to use Meal; OR update the problem statement and solution to consistently use 'Order' instead of 'Meal'. Preferably update the template to include a proper Meal class to match the problem description and solution.
